data.name: mTORC2
data.description: mTOR Complex 2; phosphorylates Akt/PKB, affects cell survival and glucose metabolism.
data.description_beginner: The second, less-studied of the two mTOR complexes. It switches on Akt and affects cell survival and how cells handle sugar.

studies.title: mTOR Signaling in Growth, Metabolism, and Disease

evidence.label: Review — secondary literature, not a new result
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: Comprehensive synthesis of mTORC1/mTORC2 signaling, growth regulation, metabolism, and disease relevance.

studies.title: Phosphorylation and regulation of Akt/PKB by the rictor-mTOR complex

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: The rictor-mTOR complex (mTORC2) directly phosphorylates Akt/PKB on Ser473, regulating cell survival.

studies.title: Rapamycin-induced insulin resistance is mediated by mTORC2 loss and uncoupled from longevity
studies.authors: Lamming DW et al.; Sabatini DM

evidence.label: Animal model
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.model_system: Mouse (in vivo glucose and insulin tolerance)
studies.finding: In mice, chronic rapamycin also disrupts mTORC2, causing insulin resistance; reduced mTORC1 signalling alone (female mTOR/mLST8 double-heterozygous mice) extended lifespan without impairing glucose homeostasis.

studies.title: Defining the role of mTOR in cancer

evidence.label: Review — secondary literature, not a new result
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: Comprehensive review arguing mTOR signaling is commonly deregulated in human cancers, laying out the rationale for rapalog trials in oncology.

studies.title: The mTOR kinase differentially regulates effector and regulatory T cell lineage commitment
studies.authors: Delgoffe GM; Powell JD et al.

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: T cells lacking mTOR fail to become normal effector cells and default toward regulatory T cells, showing mTOR is a master switch for immune cell fate.

studies.title: Rictor, a novel binding partner of mTOR, defines a rapamycin-insensitive and raptor-independent pathway that regulates the cytoskeleton
studies.authors: Sarbassov DD; Ali SM; Kim DH; Guertin DA; Latek RR; Erdjument-Bromage H; Tempst P; Sabatini DM

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: Discovery of Rictor and the SECOND mTOR complex, mTORC2. Crucially showed this complex is NOT blocked by rapamycin and does not use Raptor - it controls the cytoskeleton via PKC. This is the paper that split mTOR biology into 'two faces' at the molecular level.

studies.title: DEPTOR is an mTOR inhibitor frequently overexpressed in multiple myeloma cells and required for their survival
studies.authors: Peterson TR; Laplante M; Thoreen CC; Sancak Y; Kang SA; Kuehl WM; Gray NS; Sabatini DM

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: Identified DEPTOR as a built-in brake on BOTH mTOR complexes. The twist: in some multiple myelomas DEPTOR is overexpressed, which by relieving a feedback loop actually keeps pro-survival Akt signaling ON - a neat example of how an 'inhibitor' can be co-opted by cancer.

studies.title: Prolonged rapamycin treatment inhibits mTORC2 assembly and Akt/PKB
studies.authors: Sarbassov DD; Ali SM; Sengupta S; Sheen JH; Hsu PP; Bagley AF; Markhard AL; Sabatini DM

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: The molecular explanation for rapamycin's dark side. Short-term rapamycin only hits mTORC1, but LONG-term treatment also strips down mTORC2 in many cells, cutting Akt signaling. This is the mechanistic root of the insulin-resistance side effect later shown in mice (see Lamming 2012) - crucial for anyone dosing rapamycin for longevity.

studies.title: Active-site inhibitors of mTOR target rapamycin-resistant outputs of mTORC1 and mTORC2
studies.authors: Feldman ME; Apsel B; Uotila A; Loewith R; Knight ZA; Ruggero D; Shokat KM

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: The parallel discovery to Thoreen 2009 (same year), from the Shokat lab. Their TORKinibs (PP242, PP30) block mTOR's active site, hitting both complexes and shutting down cap-dependent translation that rapamycin misses. Together these two papers established a whole new drug class beyond rapamycin.

studies.title: mTOR at the nexus of nutrition, growth, ageing and disease

evidence.label: Review — secondary literature, not a new result
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: The flagship modern review of the whole field, from Sabatini's own lab (Nature Reviews Molecular Cell Biology). Maps 25+ years of mTOR biology - how it senses nutrients, controls growth and autophagy, and goes wrong in cancer, neurodegeneration, metabolic disease and aging. The single best orientation document for the entire Atlas.

studies.title: mTOR signaling in growth control and disease

evidence.label: Review — secondary literature, not a new result
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: The classic 2012 Cell review that became the standard reference for mTOR signaling. Comprehensive yet readable synthesis of how mTOR integrates environmental cues to control growth, and how its deregulation drives cancer, obesity, diabetes and neurodegeneration. A perfect companion to the newer 2020 review.

studies.title: Ablation in mice of the mTORC components raptor, rictor, or mLST8 reveals that mTORC2 is required for signaling to Akt-FOXO and PKCalpha, but not S6K1
studies.authors: Guertin DA; Stevens DM; Thoreen CC; Burds AA; Kalaany NY; Moffat J; Brown M; Fitzgerald KJ; Sabatini DM

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: The foundational genetic 'dissection' of the two complexes in living mice. Deleting Raptor was lethal early (mTORC1 essential); deleting Rictor or mLST8 selectively knocked out mTORC2 signaling to Akt and PKCalpha but spared S6K1. This cleanly assigned jobs to each complex and showed mLST8 is an mTORC2-specific requirement in mice.

studies.title: The Bi-steric, mTORC1-Selective Inhibitor, RMC-5552, in Advanced Solid Tumors: A Phase 1 Trial
studies.authors: Schram AM; Meyerowitz JG et al.

evidence.label: Human study
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.model_system: Human (Phase 1 dose escalation, n=57, advanced solid tumors, NCT04774952)
studies.finding: First-in-human, open-label dose-escalation trial (n=57, advanced solid tumors, no comparator arm) of a bi-steric mTORC1-selective inhibitor. Treatment-related hyperglycemia was low (4%) and not dose-limiting, alongside a 64% disease control rate. Because the trial was uncontrolled and made no head-to-head comparison against rapamycin or an ATP-site inhibitor, this is encouraging early clinical evidence consistent with the hypothesis that sparing mTORC2 reduces metabolic toxicity -- it does not establish mTORC2 sparing as the cause.

studies.title: A bi-steric mTORC1-selective inhibitor overcomes drug resistance in breast cancer
studies.authors: Meng D; Bandyopadhyay S et al.

evidence.label: Animal model
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.model_system: Human ER+/HER2- breast cancer cell lines; mouse patient-derived xenografts (PDX)
studies.finding: RMC-6272, a bi-steric molecule with >25-fold selectivity for mTORC1 over mTORC2, completely suppresses mTORC1 (hitting the rapamycin-resistant substrate 4E-BP1) and overcomes hormone- and CDK4/6-inhibitor resistance in breast cancer cell lines and PDX -- the preclinical basis for the RMC-5552 selective-inhibitor clinical program.

studies.title: A dynamic network model of mTOR signaling reveals TSC-independent mTORC2 regulation
studies.authors: Dalle Pezze P; Sonntag AG; Thien A; Prentzell MT; Gödel M; Fischer S; Neumann-Haefelin E; Huber TB; Baumeister R; Shanley DP; Thedieck K

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.model_system: Data-driven dynamic model of the insulin-mTOR network, tested in HeLa and other cell lines
studies.finding: A time-resolved, data-fitted model of the whole core insulin-mTOR network, including the mTORC1 negative feedback loop onto PI3K. Perturbing it in silico and in cells showed that TSC1-TSC2 is not a regulator of mTORC2, directly or through the feedback loop, and that mTORC2 activation runs through a PI3K variant insensitive to that loop. One of the few places where the feedback loops in the atlas are treated as a dynamical system rather than a diagram.

studies.title: A systems study reveals concurrent activation of AMPK and mTOR by amino acids
studies.authors: Dalle Pezze P; Ruf S; Sonntag AG; Langelaar-Makkinje M; Hall P; Heberle AM; Razquin Navas P; van Eunen K; Tölle RC; Schwarz JJ; Wiese H; Warscheid B; Deitersen J; Stork B; Fäßler E; Schäuble S; Hahn U; Horvatovich P; Shanley DP; Thedieck K

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.model_system: Human cell lines; amino acid re-addition time courses, quantitative proteomics and dynamic modelling
studies.finding: Adding amino acids back to starved cells switched on AMPK, PI3K and mTORC2 acutely and independently of mTORC1, at the same time as mTOR. AMPK activation ran through CaMKK-beta and, under amino acid sufficiency, AMPK kept autophagy going via ULK1. So the textbook picture of AMPK and mTORC1 as simple opposites does not hold in the first minutes after feeding - which matters for how the AMPK-ULK1 feedback arm behaves over time.

relations.mechanism: mLST8 is dispensable for mTORC1 in vivo but essential for mTORC2 - a rare clean genetic separation of the two complexes.
relations.mechanism_beginner: This protein isn't needed for mTORC1 in a living animal, but mTORC2 can't work without it – a clean genetic way to tell the two complexes apart.
relations.note: The cleanest genetic argument that the two complexes are truly separate machines.

relations.mechanism: mTORC2 is built around the same mTOR kinase as mTORC1 - the partner subunits, not the catalytic core, are what make the two complexes different.
relations.mechanism_beginner: mTORC2 is built from the very same mTOR enzyme as mTORC1 – it's the partner proteins around it that make the two complexes different.
relations.note: Three independent structures - unusually well supported for this corpus.

relations.mechanism: One of the first functions assigned to mTORC2 was shaping the cell's skeleton. In yeast it was the original TOR2 phenotype; in mammalian cells it showed that the second complex is acutely rapamycin-insensitive.
relations.mechanism_beginner: mTORC2's first known job was shaping the cell's internal skeleton – noticed precisely because rapamycin didn't block it.
relations.note: The two-complex model itself came from biochemistry (LOE2002, JAC2004, SAR2004).

relations.mechanism: mTORC2 puts the second, activating phosphate on Akt (Ser473). This is the step rapamycin eventually breaks, and a major reason, in mice, that chronic rapamycin impairs glucose tolerance (LAM2012).
relations.mechanism_beginner: mTORC2 adds the final activating tag to Akt – the same step that long-term use of the drug rapamycin eventually disrupts. In mice, that disruption is a major reason long-term rapamycin raises blood sugar.
relations.context: S473 contribution to Akt output is substrate-dependent: some Akt substrates are strongly mTORC2-dependent, others barely.
relations.note: Bridge edge between the growth-factor route and the rapamycin route.

relations.mechanism: Losing mTORC2 uncouples Akt from insulin signalling and produces glucose intolerance - and this is separable from the lifespan benefit.
relations.mechanism_beginner: Losing mTORC2 disconnects Akt from insulin signalling and can cause blood-sugar problems – a separate effect from any lifespan benefit.
relations.boundary: In mice, intermittent dosing largely spared glucose tolerance while keeping mTORC1 inhibition (ARR2015); not tested against this endpoint in humans.

relations.mechanism: In an mTOR-driven mouse liver model that progresses from steatosis to hepatocellular carcinoma, hepatic mTORC2 promoted de novo fatty-acid, sphingolipid and cardiolipin synthesis, and blocking lipid synthesis prevented the tumours.
relations.mechanism_beginner: mTORC2 also drives fat-making, which is one of the ways it is thought to help tumours grow – shown in cells and mice, not measured in patients.
relations.boundary: Single-study edge in this corpus, shown in one liver tumour model (GUR2017). Not established as a general mTORC2 function outside that setting.

relations.mechanism: Prostate tumours driven by Pten loss need mTORC2 specifically - normal prostate does not. A real therapeutic window, at least in mice.
relations.mechanism_beginner: Prostate tumours caused by losing a specific tumour-suppressor gene specifically need mTORC2 to grow – normal prostate tissue doesn't, at least in mice.

relations.mechanism: SGK1 is a second mTORC2 substrate alongside Akt, and it carries some of the functions usually credited to Akt.
relations.mechanism_beginner: SGK1 is a second target of mTORC2 alongside Akt, and it shares some of Akt's jobs.

relations.mechanism: PIP3 made by PI3K binds SIN1 and releases its hold on the kinase site - so growth-factor signalling switches mTORC2 on, not only mTORC1.
relations.mechanism_beginner: The same lipid signal that switches Akt on also switches mTORC2 on – so growth-factor signals hit both complexes.
relations.note: Thin - one supporting study for a step drawn as canonical.

relations.mechanism: Rapamycin does not touch mTORC2 in the short term - but over days it traps free mTOR and prevents new mTORC2 from being assembled.
relations.mechanism_beginner: Rapamycin doesn't touch mTORC2 right away, but over days it stops new mTORC2 from being built.
relations.boundary: Strictly time- and cell-type-dependent: absent acutely, present after prolonged exposure, and the sensitivity varies between cell lines. LAM2012 shows the same loss of mTORC2 signalling in mouse liver in vivo, so this is not a cell-culture-only phenomenon. Treating this edge as unconditional is a common error.
relations.note: THE key context-dependent edge. Should render dashed with an explicit 'chronic only' label.

relations.mechanism: Rictor defines the second complex, mTORC2, which rapamycin does not block acutely.
relations.mechanism_beginner: Rictor is what makes the second complex, mTORC2, distinct – and rapamycin doesn't block it right away.

relations.mechanism: SIN1 holds the complex together and positions the substrate; without it mTORC2 cannot phosphorylate Akt.
relations.mechanism_beginner: SIN1 holds mTORC2 together and positions its target – without it, mTORC2 can't switch Akt on.

relations.mechanism: The same active site is present in both complexes, so an ATP-competitive inhibitor cannot distinguish them.
relations.boundary: Explains the metabolic and immunological toxicity of this class relative to rapalogs; the magnitude in patients is not established from these cell-line studies.

relations.mechanism: mTORC2–Akt signalling localises to mitochondria-associated ER membranes and regulates mitochondrial physiology from there.
relations.mechanism_beginner: mTORC2 signalling also happens at a specific contact point between mitochondria and another cell structure – proof this pathway works at more than one location in the cell.
relations.boundary: Biochemical fractionation and imaging in cell lines; the functional contribution relative to plasma-membrane mTORC2 is not quantified.
